header: fix(pipeline): make the IMPLEMENT → QUALITY_GATE → REVIEW contract self-consistent (#327)
body:
- IMPLEMENT: `next` probes the task worktree with the existing
  detectImplementationDiff use case, reports implementationPresent, names
  `codeloop transition QUALITY_GATE --issue <n>` and the completion condition
  in the operator fields, and records implementationDispatchCount without
  advancing the stage.
- QUALITY_GATE dispatch: `quoted-json-comparison` is attributed per
  comparison instead of per fence, so a fixture-seeding JSON.stringify no
  longer flags an unrelated plain comparison. `jq -r` is not a JSON marker.
- QUALITY_GATE recovery: QUALITY_GATE -> PLAN is now a legal hop and the
  blocker names the re-approval walk including the plan digest re-record.
- QUALITY_GATE exit: transition REVIEW refuses when no same-round gate
  evidence is filed (nothing written), and gate-report past the gate names a
  table-derived legal walk-back.

Adds implementationDispatchCount, isLegalTransition/findLegalTransitionPath,
and regression coverage for every acceptance criterion.

Refs #327, #330

header: Merge pull request #329 from ajxcodes/fix/328
body: fix(sync): fail closed when an issue cannot be read (#328)

header: fix(sync): fail closed when an issue cannot be read (#328)
body:
`sync` performed a destructive, irreversible write on no evidence: a failed
`gh issue view` became `state: 'UNKNOWN'`, the `state !== 'CLOSED'` guard
accepted it, and the issue was closed and publicly commented on while the run
printed `Successfully synced` and exited 0.

- gateway: add a fail-closed `fetchIssueStrict` that throws unless the read
  succeeded and reported exactly OPEN or CLOSED; `fetchIssue` stays lenient for
  prompt consumers but no longer fabricates a state or defaults a missing one
  to OPEN.
- sync: authorize a write only on `state === 'OPEN'`. CLOSED is a non-mutating
  skip, an unexpected state and a failed read are reported as unreadable, and a
  gateway without the strict read refuses to write instead of falling back to
  the lenient read.
- sync: report three distinct outcomes (already closed, unreadable, closed by
  this run); an unreadable candidate or a failed write marks the run incomplete
  with a non-zero exit.
- cli: render the logs and warnings on the sync failure branch so an incomplete
  run is auditable; start-planning/start-implementation warn instead of
  swallowing the result while staying best-effort.
- sync: `--dry-run` performs the read-only scan and lists every issue it would
  close or skip, writing nothing.

Adds a stub-`gh` end-to-end suite for the unreadable, success and dry-run paths,
and repairs the shell-escaping test that only passed because of the bug.

header: Merge pull request #326 from ajxcodes/fix/301
body: fix(lifecycle): honour the descriptor contract across query, lifecycle and commit (#301)

header: fix(lifecycle): honour the descriptor contract across query, lifecycle and commit (#301)
body:
Six independent sites broke one rule: a command must act on, and describe,
exactly the tree it touched.

- run-lifecycle: provision a worktree only when a leg actually starts
  implementation (standard APPROVAL, YOLO PLAN/APPROVAL, explicit implement).
  A bare run at PLAN/REVIEW now writes nothing and leaves the checkpoint
  byte-identical. TRIAGE stays exempt via its existing early return.
- run-lifecycle: resolveWorktree no longer swallows a descriptor-save failure.
  createWorktree errors surface as WorktreeCreationError; a refused save tears
  down the just-created worktree and throws StateStorageError, so a run can no
  longer silently fall back to the root workspace or leave an orphan.
- start-planning: decide the DISCOVERY park before scaffolding. A park writes
  no plan artifacts, no .gitignore and no summary.
- transition-stage: save the checkpoint before scaffolding the plan directory,
  so a refused mutation leaves the tree byte-identical.
- get-next-action: never manufacture a checkpoint, honour --dry-run, and route
  every write through a declared write set (baseBranch, dispatch counters,
  updatedAt). The next help text now names that set instead of claiming to be
  read-only.
- commit: one shared COMMIT_EXCLUDED_PATHSPECS feeds both the printed draft and
  git rm --cached, so Files to commit (N) matches what is committed; an
  all-excluded tree refuses with an honest message. A COMMIT checkpoint with
  worktree: null is a legal root-scoped run and reports commitCwd/worktreeMode.

Absorbs #304, #307 and #319.

body:
DiscoveryReport.isPopulated was a census of `- **Key:**` bullets, so a
heading-style RCA scored 0 and parked as an "unpopulated scaffold".

- Replace the bullet census with a shape-agnostic content measure: at
  least 3 content units (substantive ## sections or key values), 150
  content chars and a 200-char document, gated by prose or bullet
  evidence.
- Accept both `**Key:**` and `**Key**:` spellings; reject pointer-only
  filler and restated headings.
- Name the measured gaps, empty sections and blank keys in the park
  message, and report the evaluated path.
- Generate the discovery prompt contract from the same constants so the
  prompt and predicate cannot drift.
- Normalize CRLF so Windows-authored reports score identically.

header: fix(app): [Phase 6] [Bug] A dispatched subagent's result has no channel back into the checkpoint: the TRIAGE disposition livelocks and the reviewer verdict is structurally unrecordable (#269) (#271)
body:
A dispatched subagent produced a result the tool had no way to file. Two gates
were unsatisfiable on the dispatch path: the TRIAGE gate re-opened forever
because the disposition was never recorded, and the reviewer subagent's
APPROVED | CHANGES_REQUESTED verdict was structurally unrecordable because
RunReviewParams.reviewOutput was declared, parsed and consumed - and supplied
by nobody.

- The triage disposition is now a first-class checkpoint field.
  TriageDisposition (src/domain/value-objects/triage-disposition.ts) carries the
  PR, the action, the timestamp and the dispositioned feedback keys; it
  round-trips through the snapshot and is cleared by reset(). The detector
  consults it, so a COMPLETED checkpoint whose PR feedback was already
  dispositioned reports the idle state instead of re-opening the TRIAGE gate.
  The livelock is a one-shot gate now.
- The detector classifies instead of counting. classifyPrFeedback
  (src/application/triage-feedback.ts) excludes the tool's own dismissal replies
  - so dismiss is no longer a trap - and the repository's own automated review
  summaries, which are status posts rather than feedback. A bot's inline
  finding stays actionable, and because the disposition records feedback keys
  rather than a timestamp, new feedback still routes.
- The exit condition is stated in the tool's own output: the TRIAGE directive,
  the idle report and the triage CLI all name it.
- codeloop review now exists and files a dispatched reviewer subagent's verdict
  through the existing RunReviewParams.reviewOutput seam, so the recorded
  verdict is the reviewer's or nothing. A parse failure or a self-declared
  SKIPPED is a hard failure that writes no checkpoint, and a CHANGES_REQUESTED
  fails the gate. The shipped skill and the CLI agree, pinned by a contract
  test.
- The recorded source never claims more than it knows: a critique-driven
  escalation is labelled reviewer-output+critique-escalation rather than
  reviewer-output.

Verified: typecheck, lint and 1381/1381 tests pass natively and under busybox
ash in Alpine; the plan's manual smoke test protocol was executed end to end
against a fake gh, with the real gh never invoked.

Co-authored-by: ajxcodes <ajxcodes@users.noreply.github.com>

header: fix(app): [Phase 6] [Bug] commentOnIssue interpolates the comment body into a shell string, so backticks are executed as commands (#262) (#268) (#268)
body:
The GitHub adapter built a shell command string with the comment body inside a
double-quoted word, escaping only the double quote. A POSIX shell still performs
command substitution inside double quotes, so a body carrying backticks or $(...)
was EXECUTED rather than posted - and the failure was silent: the shell's stderr
is piped away and the exit status stays 0.

The live symptom was codeloop sync's auto-close note, whose text wraps the
collector branch in backticks. The branch name was run as a command, the
expansion came back empty, and the posted comment read "merged via PR #261 into
." instead of naming the branch.

- The escaper is now shared, not duplicated. escapeShellQuote and shellQuote live
  in the domain layer (src/domain/value-objects/shell-quoting.ts) and the private
  lambda in execute-commit.ts is gone. The three literal prCommand assertions in
  commit-use-cases.test.ts are left unmodified and green - the tripwire proving
  the promotion was byte-identical.
- Free text never reaches a shell parser. commentOnIssue, applyLabels,
  createPullRequest and findPullRequest now travel to gh as argv elements via
  runGhArgs/execFileSync, the no-shell precedent already in this adapter.
- The residual gateway shell sites interpolate only a numeric id and a
  shellQuote'd repo slug or API path, so no value the gateway puts into a shell
  string is raw.
- sync.ts quotes the collector branch on its three shell-string paths. The
  auto-close comment names the branch again: "merged via PR #261 into
  phase/6-codeloop".
- Regression coverage: a body containing backticks, $(...), ;, && and | is
  delivered byte-for-byte and no injected command runs (fake gh harness; the
  injected marker file is never created). Architecture guards fail the build if
  the double-quote-escaping idiom or a duplicate escaper returns.

Verified: typecheck, lint and 1318/1318 tests pass; the plan's manual smoke test
protocol was executed end to end against a fake gh, with the real gh never
invoked (verified by execve tracing).

Co-authored-by: ajxcodes <ajxcodes@users.noreply.github.com>

header: fix(app): [Phase 6] [Bug] codeloop yolo never dispatches the implementer: the fast-path reaches the COMMIT gate with an empty diff, and the gates + skipped review certify it (#259) (#261)
body:
* fix(app): [Phase 6] [Bug] codeloop yolo never dispatches the implementer: the fast-path reaches the COMMIT gate with an empty diff, and the gates + skipped review certify it (#259)

The YOLO fast-path prepared an implementation but never dispatched the implementer
subagent, so the quality gates certified the untouched baseline and the pipeline
reached the COMMIT gate with an empty diff. The review then fail-opened to SKIPPED,
which the pipeline treated as a pass.

- The fast-path now measures the working tree at the IMPLEMENT to QUALITY_GATE
  boundary and parks at IMPLEMENT when no implementation is present: no state
  transition, no gate command executed, a non-green message, and the implementer
  dispatch directive - emitted by the same producer as `codeloop next`, so the two
  payloads cannot drift.
- The gate refuses to certify an unimplemented tree. It reports VACUOUS instead of
  PASSED, executes no command, consumes no retry, and never trips the circuit
  breaker. A real run gains an "Implementation : N file(s) changed" evidence line,
  so "the suite passed" and "the suite passed on a tree that contains the
  implementation" become two different statements.
- The COMMIT gate no longer describes a skipped review as a pass. The advisory
  fail-open of the review itself is preserved unchanged.
- The scaffolded execution summary no longer pre-claims COMPLETED, PASSED or
  APPROVED for stages that never ran - in the template and in its embedded fallback
  copy, guarded by a drift test that reads the template from disk.
- The park refuses to point an implementer directive at an empty plan, and the
  invariant is cross-mode: no path advances past IMPLEMENT without implementation
  evidence.

Verified: typecheck, lint and 1158/1158 tests pass, and the plan's manual smoke
test protocol (phases A-H) was executed by the quality-gate subagent.

Follow-ups, out of scope here: the fast-path never dispatches the planner either,
so an adhoc run still implements a blank scaffold; and --plan-path is not
implemented at all.

* fix(triage): PR review triage must not report a dismissal it did not perform

Found while triaging PR #261 (issue #259): the triage machinery could claim a
dismissal it never performed, read only a third of the review feedback, and
misread the severity of every comment a review bot wrote.

- The `dismiss` route wrapped every thread in a single try, so one rate limit
  aborted the whole batch; the CLI then printed an unqualified
  `✓ Triage Action : DISMISS`. Each item is now isolated, and the outcome is
  reported per surface - complete, partial, failed, or nothing dismissed. A
  dismissal that handled nothing is never green.
- The route resolved only review threads, so PR conversation comments were
  unreachable. On PR #261, 18 of 24 conversation comments sat on files with no
  inline counterpart and were never answered. Conversation comments are now
  plumbed (id and surface) and answered, skipping feedback already answered
  inline in the same run.
- The severity classifier matched only bracket forms, so the markdown markers
  review bots actually emit (CRITICAL, SUGGESTION, INFO) were invisible: all
  52 bot comments on PR #261 classified as `general`, and a genuine CRITICAL
  would have been treated as non-blocking.
- The comment fetch never passed --paginate, so 45 of 105 comments were never
  read - including the reviews surface, the only source of a CHANGES_REQUESTED
  classification.

Verified: typecheck, lint and 1185/1185 tests pass, and the plan's manual smoke
test protocol (phases A-H) was executed by the quality-gate subagent.

* fix(triage): the dismiss route must remember what it already answered

Exercising the newly-fixed dismiss route against PR #261 showed it
re-answering every conversation comment on every run - it replied to 51 of
53, and the 49 redundant replies had to be cleaned up by hand. The route had
no cross-run memory of its own work.

- "Already answered" is now derived from the PR's current state, so it
  survives across runs: an inline comment is answered when its review thread
  is resolved (the gateway fetched `isResolved` and then discarded it), and a
  conversation comment is answered when another comment references its id.
  The author is never consulted, so human feedback is not swallowed.
- The dismissal report distinguishes replied, skipped (already answered),
  skipped (duplicate feedback), ignored (own dismissal reply), ignored
  (unmarked prior answer) and failed - and the nothing-dismissed outcome
  still prints its counters, so a run that skipped everything stays visible.
- Severity markers are now anchored to the comment's leading marker, so a
  body that merely quotes one is no longer classified by it, and an INFO
  comment no longer renders as GENERAL.
- A deleted tracked file is now pinned by a test, so a deletion-only tree
  cannot silently look unimplemented.

Verified: typecheck, lint and 1197/1197 tests pass.

* test(worktree): assert the -b flag position, not a substring of the path

The existing-branch case asserted that the whole `git worktree add` command
string did not contain "-b", but the command embeds a mkdtemp worktree path.
When the random suffix starts with "b" the path reads
/tmp/agyloop-test-wt-bLeg0o, and "-wt-b" matches - so the assertion mis-fired
on a command the manager had emitted correctly. It landed on PR #261's CI.

The flag is positional: it is the token immediately after `git worktree add `.
The assertions now check that position, and a new deterministic case builds a
worktree path containing "-b" on purpose, so the condition that used to depend
on randomness is now pinned. The manager itself is unchanged.

Verified: typecheck, lint and 1198/1198 tests pass, and the target file passes
100 consecutive runs with no failure.

* docs(detect-diff): explain that an unresolvable base ref is a fallback, not a failure

The `git diff` probe's non-zero-exit check returned null with no comment,
while the sibling `git status` probe carried a "fail closed" note - so the
branch read as a failure path when it is in fact an expected condition: the
base ref may not exist in this repository, and the caller retries against HEAD
rather than failing hard.

Comment only - no behaviour changes.

* refactor(triage): split performDismissal into its two jobs

performDismissal was 263 lines interleaving the inline review-thread loop
and the PR conversation-comment loop, with nine shared counters and two
shared sets that one job wrote and the other read. Extract each job into its
own private helper and leave performDismissal as the orchestrator: guards,
shared state, the two helpers, the failure warning, the report.

Purely structural. The report shape, the counters, the rendered operator
output, the four outcome classes and the failure and surface ordering are
byte-identical - verified by diffing the rendered output of the pre- and
post-refactor builds across the full scenario matrix.

* fix(triage): a resolved review thread is not proof that it was answered

The dismissal route's cross-run memory decided "was this feedback already
answered?" from the thread's resolution state. That inference is false for
this repository's review bot: the Critique Reviewer action auto-resolves the
threads it creates, so a resolved thread can be entirely unanswered.

Measured on PR #261: 64 threads, all resolved, but only 30 contained a
reply - the other 34 were never answered by anyone, and the route skipped
them all, reporting "0 replied, 0 resolved, 64 skipped (already answered)".
Two of the 34 carried suggestions this branch had already actioned.

"Already answered" now means evidence that a reply was made: the thread
carries a dismissal marker, or the tool's historic signature. A resolved
thread without one is answered, and is not resolved again - it is already
closed. The tool never answers its own replies, and the report shape and
the rendered operator output are unchanged.

Verified: typecheck, lint and 1203/1203 tests pass; a read-only dry run
against PR #261's live state gives 34 replied and 30 skipped, against 0
replied and 64 skipped before the fix.

header: fix(preflight): [Phase 6] [Bug] Pre-flight halts on evidence of delivery, not on a branch name (#226) (#246)
body:
* fix(preflight): [Phase 6] [Bug] Pre-flight halts on evidence of delivery, not on a branch name (#226)

`codeloop plan 226` hard-halted with "PR for task #226 is already merged into
phase/6-codeloop" even though issue #226 is OPEN and unimplemented.

`findPullRequest` binds a PR to an issue by head-branch regex, and PR #228 --
a one-line test-mock fix for an Alpine CI failure that was merely *developed
on* a branch named `task/226` -- matched issue #226. `RunPreFlightCheckUseCase`
then saw "merged + branch matches the task/<n> convention" and refused to
schedule the work.

A branch name is a naming convention, not a delivery claim, and this repo's
own history conflates the two routinely. So a merged PR now halts the pipeline
only when its **body** carries a GitHub closing keyword for that issue
(`Closes/Fixes/Resolves #<n>`), which is exactly where `execute-commit.ts`
writes `Closes #${issueId}`. A merged PR bound only by branch name or a
`(#<n>)` title cross-reference is disregarded loudly and execution proceeds.

The halt is not weakened -- the trigger is strictly *higher* than the branch
regex it replaces, so every genuine delivery still halts. The non-delivery
path emits a multi-line warning naming the PR, its title, its head branch,
the issue's still-OPEN state, and the operator action.

Adds `prAssertsIssueDelivery` / `branchNameReferencesIssue` as a pure domain
module, plumbs the PR body through the gateway, and gives `findPullRequest` a
new highest-precedence tier so it returns the *delivering* PR when one exists.

Tests: 1013 pass (was 993; +20, 0 regressions). Non-vacuity verified -- reverting
the one-line trigger turns 5 tests red, including the headline regression.

Refs #226

* fix(state): [Phase 6] [Bug] State mutation contracts: stale gate pauses, dry-run/rejected-path mutations, authoritative checkpoint resolution, and installer failure reporting (#226) (#246)

Restores one honest answer to two questions the lifecycle got wrong in eight
places: which checkpoint is authoritative, and is this invocation allowed to
write it or halt on it.

D1 - a `COMPLETED` pipeline retained a stale `COMMIT` pause forever.
`StateMachine.transition()` auto-consumes pauses only when they are NOT in
`HUMAN_WAIT_GATES`, and there was no bound for the terminal stage, so
`ExecuteCommitUseCase`'s `COMMIT -> COMPLETED` persisted
`{ currentStage: COMPLETED, pausedAtGate: COMMIT }` that no later transition
could clear: `status` reported a finished pipeline that was also waiting on a
human, and `totalHumanWaitMs` stayed 0 forever. Fixed in the domain, not in the
use case: entering `COMPLETED` resolves and banks the pause, because
`execute-commit.ts` and `transition-stage.ts` are the only call sites that reach
it and both are covered by one rule.

D2 - `implement --dry-run` provisioned a real worktree. The guardrail at
`start-implementation.ts` gated only on `noWorktree`, unlike the pre-sync and
the final save in the same method, and unlike `RunLifecycleUseCase`
.resolveWorktree`, which already returns null under `--dry-run`. A dry run
therefore created `.worktrees/<id>` plus a branch with NO checkpoint referencing
it. `dryRun` is now part of `skipWorktree` in both `start-implementation.ts` and
`transition-stage.ts`.

D3 - a REJECTED transition provisioned a worktree. The worktree auto-provision
guardrail in `transition-stage.ts` ran BEFORE the transition validity check, so
`transition IMPLEMENT` from `PLAN` in mode `plan` threw
`Invalid lifecycle transition` yet had already created `.worktrees/adhoc`.
The guardrail now runs only after `sm.transition()` proves the target legal,
so nothing is created on the failure path and nothing is persisted on it.

D4 - `transition --dry-run` wrote state and reported success. The CLI built the
`TransitionStageUseCase` call without forwarding `options.dryRun`, leaving the
use case'S existing `if (!params.dryRun)` guard dead code on that path; a dry
run printed `✓ Transitioned to [DISCOVERY]` AND wrote `.agyloop/state.json`.
The flag is forwarded and the success line now carries the `[dry-run] ` prefix,
matching the existing `resume`/`halt` convention.

D5/D6 - one shared task-checkpoint resolver (`src/application/
resolve-task-checkpoint.ts`). Before it, `status`, `resume`, `next`,
`branch-info`, `halt`, `transition`, `implement` and `plan` each re-derived the
root-vs-task question on their own, so with work in
`.agyloop/tasks/<n>.json` the CLI reported `[INITIALIZED]` off a root file that
was not even read, and a bare `codeloop resume` declared "nothing to resume"
while the task sat paused at `COMMIT`. One resolver now answers which
checkpoint is authoritative for `status` (D5) and, crucially, for `resume`'s
READ AND WRITE (D6) - resolving for display while saving through the root file
would have been the same defect in a new shape. An optional `StateRepository
.forIssue?` port method and `FileStateRepository.forIssue()` make the scoped
repository address load, save and path consistently. A corrupt or unreadable
checkpoint is dropped from the candidates rather than crashing the scan, and
`resume` reports an unreadable winner instead of pretending the checkpoint does
not exist.

D7 - `bin/verify-install.sh` exited 2 on a missing manifest and printed
"Invalid JSON syntax" for a file that did not exist. Under `set -eu` a
`VAR="$(jq ...)"` assignment aborted the script with jq's exit status before
its own FAILED summary ran. Steps 3 and 4 are now guarded on `[ -f ]`, the
extractions carry `|| true`, so a missing manifest reports the actionable
`setup-symlink.sh` hint and exits with the script's own documented 1, while a
genuinely malformed file still reports a syntax error correctly.

D8 was already landed in `4873ea1` (pre-flight halts on evidence of delivery,
not on a branch name). Reviewer-found follow-up on it is not part of this diff.

Review fix - the new resolver initially let a corrupt task checkpoint crash the
scan; the reviewer caught it and the fix landed in this commit with
non-vacuity evidence.

Tests: 1079 pass (993 baseline; +86 across D1-D7 and the review fix, 0
failures). Build, typecheck, lint all clean. The Alpine CI leg passed live
under `act` + rootless podman (node:24-alpine with jq installed). Non-vacuity
verified per defect by reverting each fix and observing the named tests go red.

Refs #226

header: fix(state): [Phase 6] [Bug] Task worktree state bleed: discoverWorkspaceRoot resolves state to the MAIN worktree, so worktree runs read/write the root checkpoint (#244) (#245)
fix(app): [Phase 6] [Bug] Lifecycle re-entry contract: YOLO re-entry after the DISCOVERY park skips RCA, and next --issue on COMPLETED silently resets the task (#237) (#243)
body:
Two defects, both instances of the lifecycle advancing a stage
without its work actually being done.

Defect 1: start-planning advanced DISCOVERY -> PLAN unconditionally on
re-entry, so a yolo re-run bypassed the RCA park. The re-entry decision
now goes through a single chokepoint
(src/application/lifecycle-reentry-policy.ts) with two rule tables and
fail-closed defaults. Evidence is content-based
(src/domain/value-objects/discovery-report.ts), not existence-based,
because FilePlanGenerator always writes a plan file when scaffolding --
so 'a discovery file exists' is trivially true for an untouched template.

The predicate is calibrated against this repository's real discovery
reports, not against the template. Measured over artifacts/plans: 0%
false negatives (was ~80%, when a key whose value is an indented sub-list
scored as unfilled and quoted scaffolds inside fenced blocks were
counted), while a pristine scaffold still parks. --skip-discovery is the
explicit, audited escape hatch and is now the only one.

Defect 2: 'next --issue <n>' treated an explicit issue on a COMPLETED
checkpoint as authorization to sm.reset(), destroying it, and reached PLAN
inline while bypassing the planDir precondition enforced by
TransitionStageUseCase -- producing the forbidden
{ currentStage: PLAN, planDir: null } snapshot. next is now
non-destructive by default (zero writes); --restart is the only reset path
and it lands at DISCOVERY, never PLAN; open-PR review feedback routes to
TRIAGE via the shared shouldRouteToTriage predicate that
RunLifecycleUseCase also consults. Grep-verifiable: no
transition(STAGE_PLAN) remains in get-next-action.ts.

ALLOWED_TRANSITIONS is deliberately NOT widened: the honest restore path
already exists in three legal hops, and letting 'transition COMPLETED'
succeed from IMPLEMENT would mark unverified work complete. The restore
is a no-op + advisory, never a worktree teardown.

A re-entry also no longer orphans the checkpoint's existing plan directory:
the scaffold no longer repoints an already-populated planDir.

Tests: 918 -> 985. Regression tests verified non-vacuous by mutation
testing -- reverting either headline fix produces concrete failures, and
the sentinel gate use case fires.

header: fix(reviewer): [Phase 6] [Bug] AI review fabricates CHANGES_REQUESTED when no reviewer output or critique report is produced, failing clean headless yolo runs (#236) (#238)
fix(yolo): checkpoint bug-issue DISCOVERY park and guard wrong-stage gates (#234) (#235)
body:
`codeloop yolo` hard-crashed (exit 1) on any bug-classified issue. Bug
issues are intentionally parked at DISCOVERY for RCA, but executeYoloMode
had no leg for that stage: the implementation step was silently skipped by
its stage guard while the quality-gate call was unguarded, so
RunQualityGateUseCase threw InvalidTransitionError from the wrong stage.
Nothing was checkpointed and no resume guidance was printed, stranding
pipeline state (and, in the issue-bearing variant, orphaning a worktree
that later bricked `next` via Zero Direct Root Mutation).

- constants: add NOTE_YOLO_PARKED_AT_DISCOVERY with codeloop next/resume
  guidance
- run-lifecycle: DISCOVERY park leg in executeYoloMode (mirrors standard
  mode); whitelist guard around the quality-gate call
  (IMPLEMENT/QUALITY_GATE/COMMIT/COMPLETED) and the review call
  (QUALITY_GATE/REVIEW/COMPLETED) that checkpoints instead of throwing;
  persist the worktree descriptor immediately after resolveWorktree
- cli: surface result.message on the yolo early-halt path; catch
  InvalidTransitionError with standard checkpoint/resume guidance

Behavior deltas (intentional): bug-issue yolo now exits 0 on the
DISCOVERY park, and `actionOnTrip: warn` breaker results surface as a
warning + exit 1 instead of the misleading "gates passed" + exit 0.

Tested: 906/906 (baseline 897 + 9 new: yolo discovery park A1-A5,
run-quality-gate DISCOVERY pin, and e2e cli-yolo-discovery C1-C3).
build/typecheck/lint clean; smoke S1-S6 green.

Closes #234

header: fix(gate): guard DOCKER_HOST socket resolution in container gate detection (#232) (#233)
body:
resolveContainerSocket() returned process.env.DOCKER_HOST verbatim, so a
stale or absent socket path selected the act container gate and hard-failed
the pipeline on a dead daemon instead of skipping the gate.

- strip the unix:// scheme (or bare absolute path) and verify the endpoint
  with statSync().isSocket() before returning it; warn and fall through to
  /var/run/docker.sock when the path is missing or not a socket
- pass non-unix schemes (tcp://, ssh://, http(s)://) through unchanged
- add T1-T8 coverage: dead path => null, non-socket file => null, live
  socket control, tcp pass-through, act-gate skip in RunQualityGateUseCase,
  and the ResolveSubagentUseCase empirical-verification fallback (AC-5)

header: fix(state): stop caching failed git root resolution and protect .agyloop symlink in scaffolds (#221) (#231)
body:
Defect 1 - workspace-root resolution failed open:
- FileStateRepository.discoverWorkspaceRoot() no longer caches the cwd fallback
  when both git probes fail, so a transient git failure can no longer pin
  workspaceRoot to the cwd for the process lifetime (state split-brain).

Defect 2 - consumer scaffolds lacked the symlink ignore rule:
- INIT_GITIGNORE_RULES now emits the symlink-safe pair: a bare `.agyloop`
  (matches the mode-120000 symlink created in worktrees) immediately re-included
  by `!.agyloop/` so `.agyloop/config.json` stays trackable.
- FileProjectScaffolder keeps the managed pair instead of swapping the bare entry
  for granular rules, and orders the `!.agyloop/` negation after its bare
  counterpart so the directory is not re-excluded.

Tests: full suite green (889) - adds coverage for the un-cached failure path and
the symlink-safe scaffold contract.

Closes #221

header: feat(quota): add halt inbound channel for 429 recovery (#224)
fix(hardening): harden installer, quota pauses, branch detection, prompt guards (#218) (#219)
body:
* fix(hardening): harden installer, quota pauses, branch detection, prompt guards (#218)

Operational polish pass addressing six live anomalies from Phase 6 runs.

OpenCode integration installer:
- auto-register command.codeloop in the active opencode.jsonc/opencode.json,
  idempotently, via parse-merge-atomic-write with a .codeloop.bak backup;
  refuse rather than corrupt on unparseable, non-object, or BOM-prefixed input
- install the skill at the layout OpenCode actually reads
  (<config>/skills/codeloop/SKILL.md) with metadata["opencode/slash"]
- replace existsSync with an lstatSync-first sweep so dangling symlinks are
  detected and unlinked before linking (force was a documented no-op)
- canonicalize the source to the primary worktree root, copying with a
  degradedReason instead of linking into an ephemeral .worktrees/<id> path

Quota exhaustion (429 / RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED):
- add QuotaExhaustedError and a pure classifyQuotaExhaustion so the provider
  signal is not destroyed at the runner's throw boundary
- persist the CIRCUIT_BREAKER pause: handleCircuitBreakerTrip called
  pauseAtGate without stateRepo.save, so the checkpoint on disk stayed null
  and the next invocation re-entered the failing stage with no context
- add FailoverAgentRunner to invoke a configured fallback exactly once on
  quota errors, leaving genuine failures unmasked
- surface a distinct exit code for a quota halt, documented in printHelp

Default branch resolution:
- InitProjectUseCase.detectGit falls back through the current local branch
  (rejecting a detached HEAD) and common candidates before defaulting to main,
  and reads origin/HEAD from the resolved remote rather than a hardcoded one

Interactive prompt guarding:
- compute promptsAllowed once in the composition root and thread it through
  commit, review and the lifecycle use cases; fix interactiveCommit: true,
  which was hardcoded and could block forever on a non-TTY stdin
- give ReadlineConfirmationPrompt a TTY self-guard that returns the safe
  default before constructing a readline interface
- split the commit --json diagnostic so it no longer claims a non-interactive
  terminal on an interactive one

Gates: build, typecheck, lint clean; 817/817 tests pass.

Co-Authored-By: CodeLoop Pipeline <noreply@agyloop.local>

* fix(triage): fail-closed state guard, POSIX launchers, git 2.5x worktree recovery

Three bugs surfaced by running the suite in a podman container where the host
passed 817/817 and the container passed 813/817. All three are invisible to CI,
which only runs ubuntu-latest.

State isolation guard fails open (safety):
- validateSmokeTestIsolation compared stateFilePath (resolved from cwd) against
  discoverWorkspaceRoot(__dirname). When git fails -- a container whose .git
  indirection points outside the mount, a CI tarball, a broken worktree gitdir --
  both resolutions fall back to their cwd, diverge, and the guard silently
  disables itself. No throw, no warning.
- Under node --test a stray save()/reset()/resetAll() could overwrite or unlink
  real .agyloop state, and cli.ts wires SIGINT/SIGTERM to resetAll().
- Invert to a fail-closed predicate: only a path provably inside the OS temp
  sandbox may be mutated, with the workspace root as a negative veto. The
  decision no longer depends on git, so discovery failure can no longer disable
  protection. Also covers workspaceResetTargets(), which resetTask/resetAll
  derive their deletions from.

Shell launchers were not POSIX despite declaring they were:
- bin/codeloop and bin/agyloop are headed "POSIX Shell Launcher" but used a
  bash shebang, ${BASH_SOURCE[0]}, and &>/dev/null. Under BusyBox they fail with
  exit 127 "env: can't execute 'bash'"; under dash &> parses as background, so
  the Node.js guard fires falsely.
- Same class in setup-symlink.sh and verify-install.sh, which no test covered.
  Convert all four: #!/bin/sh, $0, >/dev/null 2>&1, [[ ]] -> [ ], == -> =.
- Dropped set -o pipefail: not POSIX, and none of the four scripts has a
  pipeline. New static tests pin the shebang and the bash-only constructs.
- Add a non-blocking posix-shell CI job running the suite in Alpine. Lands with
  continue-on-error and outside tag.needs so a new network-dependent job cannot
  block releases; promotion recipe is in the job comment.

Worktree recovery was dead code on modern git:
- The git worktree add failure path matched only "already checked out at", but
  git 2.53 emits "is already used by worktree at". Recovery was unreachable,
  which blocked a live pipeline transition during triage.
- Resolve the holder from git worktree list --porcelain first (a stable format,
  unlike error prose) and widen the text match as fallback. The porcelain result
  was already being fetched and discarded.
- A prunable holder is now pruned and retried rather than adopted as a
  descriptor pointing at a deleted directory.

Gates: build, typecheck, lint and actionlint clean; 837/837 tests pass on the
host and in a bash-less node:24-alpine container.

Co-Authored-By: CodeLoop Pipeline <noreply@agyloop.local>

* fix(worktree): restore dead .agyloop symlink eviction guard (#102 regression)

`.agyloop` is a symlink pointing at an absolute, developer-specific path. It was
committed in 7cd82b3 and is therefore present in PR #219, so anyone checking out
that commit gets a dangling symlink into their own filesystem layout.

This is the bug class of #101/#102, which was already fixed once in 399578a and
has since regressed through two independent defects.

The eviction guard never ran:
- `git rm --cached -rf .agyloop node_modules artifacts || true` aborts with
  "fatal: pathspec 'node_modules' did not match any files" as soon as any one
  pathspec is untracked, and it aborts before removing .agyloop. The `|| true`
  swallowed the non-zero exit, so the guard silently did nothing.
  Now uses --ignore-unmatch and the argv form, and fails closed on a genuine
  error rather than swallowing it.

The .gitignore protection was gone:
- 399578a added a bare `.agyloop` entry. 19f00f7 (feat(init) #216/#217) replaced
  it with granular `.agyloop/state.json`, `.agyloop/tasks/`, ... rules. Those
  never protected the symlink: git stores it as mode 120000, a file, so a
  `.agyloop/...` rule cannot match it and `git add -A` stages it freely.
  The bare entry is restored, which also makes it unstageable in the first place.

The existing #102 test asserted only that the command string was issued, with a
mock pre-seeded to exit 0. It never modelled an unmatched pathspec, so the broken
command satisfied it trivially -- it asserted the call, not the effect. New tests
assert the argv form, the presence of --ignore-unmatch, the absence of `|| true`,
and fail-closed behaviour.

Verified in an isolated scratch repo: the old command leaves .agyloop staged and
exits 128 (0 once `|| true` swallows it); the new command evicts it and exits 0.

Gates: build, typecheck, lint clean; 839/839 tests pass.

Co-Authored-By: CodeLoop Pipeline <noreply@agyloop.local>

* fix(lifecycle): make gate pauses consumable, visible, and clearable

A persisted CIRCUIT_BREAKER pause was effectively a dead end: it never cleared
itself, no real command consulted it, and the recovery hint we shipped pointed
at a command that cannot clear it.

Sticky pause:
- pauseAtGate only records the first pause and transition() never cleared
  pausedAtGate, so once a gate-retry breaker or quota pause tripped, the
  checkpoint claimed "waiting for a human" through every subsequent stage
  transition forever.
- transition() now consumes a pause at a non-human gate, since reaching a later
  stage is proof the blocking condition resolved. HUMAN_WAIT_GATES
  (APPROVAL/COMMIT/TRIAGE) is deliberately preserved -- those exist to wait for
  a human and transition-stage depends on it.
- resumeFromGate() also clears a checkpoint that recorded a gate with no
  timestamp, which would otherwise be un-resumable.

The resume hint we shipped was wrong:
- QUOTA_RESUME_COMMAND was 'codeloop next', but resumeFromGate() is reachable
  only from transition and triage -- `next` never cleared a pause. printHelp()
  told users to run a command that did nothing.
- Adds `codeloop resume`, which calls resumeFromGate(), checkpoints the wait
  into totalHumanWaitMs, and honours --dry-run and --json.
- resumeFromGate() moved out of the timestamp branch so clearing no longer
  depends on a timestamp being present.

Invisible pauses:
- RunLifecycleUseCase now emits an advisory (never blocking) notice when the
  checkpoint it loaded was already paused, at the single chokepoint every mode
  flows through, so plan/implement/yolo/default all surface it. Advisory
  because implement is the documented resume path; blocking would strand it.
- next --json now carries the pause. The check previously sat after the --json
  early-return, so the one call the agent harness is told to make never saw it.
  stdout stays a single pure JSON document; the warning goes to stderr.
- status now renders the gate, the timestamp and a recovery hint; the data was
  already returned and never displayed.
- Documented in skills/agyloop/SKILL.md and integrations/opencode/codeloop-
  skill.md, since discoverability is the fix: next reports a pause, resume
  clears it.

Not changed: AgentRunnerPort stays unwired. codeloop is a plugin manifest -- the
host IDE spawns subagents and the CLI emits invoke_subagent payloads, per
skills/agyloop/SKILL.md's Zero Direct Root Mutation contract. A provider 429
therefore never crosses a TypeScript boundary in this architecture, which is why
FailoverAgentRunner and exit code 2 remain forward-looking rather than wired.
Wiring them would invert the contract rather than fix a bug.

Gates: build, typecheck, lint clean; 863/863 tests pass on host and in a
bash-less node:24-alpine container.
